slot.brief: A nucleus undergoes alpha decay; compute energy released using given binding energies of parent, daughter and alpha, then find kinetic energy of the alpha particle.

stem: A stationary $^{232}_{92}\text{U}$ nucleus undergoes $\alpha$-decay to $^{228}_{90}\text{Th}$. Their total binding energies are $1755.5$ MeV, $1733.0$ MeV and $28.3$ MeV for the parent, daughter and $\alpha$-particle, respectively. Taking nuclear masses proportional to mass numbers, the kinetic energy of the $\alpha$-particle is

verdicts.working: The decay energy is Q = 1733.0 + 28.3 − 1755.5 = 5.8 MeV. By momentum conservation, the alpha-particle receives the fraction 228/232 of Q, so Tα = 5.8 × 228/232 = 5.7 MeV.

working:
$$Q = 1733.0 + 28.3 - 1755.5 = 5.8\ \text{MeV}$$
$$p_{\alpha}=p_d,\quad K_{\alpha}=Q\frac{m_d}{m_{\alpha}+m_d}=5.8\frac{228}{232}=5.7\ \text{MeV}$$

Independent check: The decay energy is Q = 1733.0 + 28.3 − 1755.5 = 5.8 MeV. By momentum conservation, the alpha-particle receives the fraction 228/232 of Q, so Tα = 5.8 × 228/232 = 5.7 MeV.
